They also recognize that the failure to file an undertaking does not preclude an appellant from pursuing an appeal unless, as a result of doing so, the appellant accepts the benefits of the judgment. To the extent that our opinion in City of Portland holds that an appellant’s voluntary compliance with a judgment is sufficient — standing alone — to foreclose an appeal, we disavow it. See Kambury v. DaimlerChrysler Corp., 173 Or App 372, 379, 21 P3d 1089 (2001) (adhering to stare decisis “unless error is plainly shown to exist”); Newell v. Weston, 156 Or App 371, 380, 965 P2d 1039 (1998), rev den 329 Or 318 (1999) (same). Following Edwards, Staiger, and Cottrell, we hold that plaintiffs’ compliance with the judgment in this case does not bar them from pursuing their appeal. In this case no proper finding of guilt of any charge having been made by the jury, there can be no modification by the court predicated on a finding of guilt of a lesser included offense. We disavow the determinations made in People v Brown (21 AD2d 738) and in People v Zimmerman (supra) to the extent that they are inconsistent herewith. The judgment convicting defendant of attempted manslaughter, second degree is reversed and the indictment dismissed.
